edges.description: EXOC3L2 functions in trafficking of post-Golgi vesicles to the plasma membrane; its loss is presumed to impair that trafficking. No study demonstrates the trafficking defect in a patient cell, so the link is inferred rather than shown.
The authors suggest EXOC3L2 takes part in VEGFR2 recycling and localization in endothelial cells; the trafficking step itself was not shown.
edges.target: Defective Endothelial VEGFR2 Signaling and Directional Migration

edges.description: How EXOC3L2 loss disturbs cerebellar and fourth-ventricle development is unknown.
How EXOC3L2 loss disturbs kidney development is unknown.

In mice, deleting Exoc3l2 from endothelial and hematopoietic lineages reproduces the brain anomalies, including in the cerebellum, but neural progenitor numbers were unchanged and the route is not known.
edges.source: Defective Endothelial VEGFR2 Signaling and Directional Migration

edges.description: Abnormal hindbrain development produces the Dandy-Walker malformation.
Abnormal cerebellar development produces vermis hypoplasia.
Abnormal kidney development produces renal dysplasia.
Abnormal kidney development produces enlarged, hyperechogenic fetal kidneys.
Abnormal kidney development produces the renal enlargement seen on fetal ultrasound.
Oligohydramnios accompanies the renal malformation, consistent with reduced fetal urine production, though urine output was not measured.
Pulmonary hypoplasia accompanies the oligohydramnios, consistent with the usual consequence of reduced amniotic fluid; the source does not state the link.
Conditional knockout embryos show cerebellar morphological anomalies.
edges.limitations: Embryos die in utero with hemorrhage and heart defects not reported in patients, the brain phenotype was not characterized as a Dandy-Walker malformation, and the kidney was not examined.
